peripherals: Display controller (ST7735S/ST7789 via SPI or I2C)
notes: The project already uses a clean NATIVE_TEST dual-implementation architecture, which isolates hardware-specific code well.
hal_system is trivial to migrate: replace millis()/delay() with esp_timer_get_time()/vTaskDelay().
hal_input is medium difficulty: need to implement GPIO edge detection and debouncing directly since esp-idf has no built-in button library like M5Unified.
hal_power_key is medium-high: AXP192 is on I2C; need either an existing esp-idf AXP192 driver or manual I2C register access to replace M5.Power.getKeyState().

hal_display and its submodules are the hardest part: M5GFX/M5Canvas is a large graphics library. Options are (1) port LovyanGFX (which M5GFX is based on) to esp-idf, or (2) rewrite drawing primitives using esp-idf LCD driver + a lightweight software renderer. The native test implementations exist but are software-rendered and slow.
hal_layout and hal_input_double_click are pure C with no hardware dependencies and require zero changes.
The display stack uses 8-bit RGB332 color depth via M5Canvas to save RAM; any replacement must support this optimization or provide equivalent memory-efficient framebuffer management.
Chinese font support (U8G2 format subset) is loaded in hal_display_adv.cpp; this depends on M5GFX's U8g2font renderer and would need a replacement font rendering strategy.

migrationNotes: framework must change from 'arduino' to 'espidf' (or 'arduino,espidf' for hybrid)
Arduino-specific libraries (M5Unified, M5GFX, ArduinoJson) are incompatible with pure esp-idf; must be replaced with esp-idf equivalents or vendor SDKs
M5Stick-C Arduino board definition is not valid under esp-idf; must switch to a raw ESP32 board (e.g., esp32dev) or create a custom board JSON with correct flash/PSRAM settings
board_build.partitions path must point to an esp-idf partition table CSV or use esp-idf's default partitions
Arduino core debug macros (CORE_DEBUG_LEVEL) are not available in esp-idf; replace with ESP_LOGx levels
Arduino String/Stream classes and HardwareSerial APIs must be replaced with esp-idf UART driver or C++ standard types
setup()/loop() paradigm must be replaced with app_main() and FreeRTOS tasks
ArduinoJson is Arduino-only; replace with cJSON or nlohmann/json for esp-idf
M5Unified/M5GFX depend on Arduino core; for esp-idf use LovyanGFX with esp-idf support or write a thin driver layer
Linker wrap flags (-Wl,--wrap,...) remain valid but should be verified against newlib in esp-idf toolchain
fno-exceptions and fno-rtti are valid but must be explicitly enabled in esp-idf CMake or sdkconfig
native test environment (env:native) is independent and does not require changes for esp-idf migration

output.framework: ESP-IDF via PlatformIO (espressif32 platform, m5stick-c board)
missingPieces: No actual application code (main.c is an empty app_main stub)
No component-level CMakeLists.txt with explicit source lists and include dirs
No Kconfig.projbuild or custom Kconfig for project-specific configuration options
No partition table CSV or partition configuration in sdkconfig
No bootloader customization or secure boot configuration
No existing drivers or hardware abstraction layer for M5Stick-C peripherals (ST7789 display, PMU, IMU, etc.)
No FreeRTOS task structure or event loop setup
No logging or system initialization code beyond the empty stub
No test code in test/ directory (directory exists but is empty)
No CI/CD configuration or build scripts for pure ESP-IDF (currently tied to PlatformIO)
No sdkconfig.defaults to share base configuration across environments
No flash size or memory layout configuration review
No dependency management for external components (idf_component.yml)

uiModules: ui_core.c/h — animation engine, main loop dispatch, lifecycle
ui_draw_list.c — list frame rendering (appearance, items, selector, overlays)
ui_anim_row.h — reusable animated row list utility
ui_context.h — global state singleton with backward-compat macros
ui_dispatch.c — type-specific dispatch table for enter/draw/measure/destroy
appModules: app_menu.c — builds the Xerintosh menu tree
app_input.c — maps hardware buttons to UI navigation
ui_task.c — FreeRTOS kernel task wrapper for UI loop
screenAssumptions: RGB565 API color constants, 8-bit RGB332 hardware canvas for RAM savings
COLOR_BG=0x0000 black, COLOR_FG=0xFFFF white, COLOR_ACCENT=0x07E0 green, COLOR_RED=0xF800
Native test build uses 80x160 software framebuffer with 6x8 bitmap font
notes: All M5GFX/M5Unified dependencies are isolated to the HAL layer (src/hal/); no direct GFX calls exist in ui/ or app/
The Xerintosh UI framework is fully portable — it only uses hal_display.h and hal_input.h abstractions
Migration strategy: reimplement HAL backends while keeping API signatures identical; no UI/App code changes required
Font migration requires replacing lgfx::U8g2font with new platform's renderer; hal_get_cn_font() must return compatible pointer
Color depth change (e.g., from RGB332 to RGB565 or 24-bit) only affects hal_display_fb.cpp and hal_display_draw.cpp
Screen size assumptions are centralized in hal_screen.h via SCREEN_WIDTH/SCREEN_HEIGHT macros; apps use HAL_LAYOUT macros that auto-adapt
The 8-bit M5Canvas was chosen specifically to save 12.8KB RAM for Classic BT SPP + UI coexistence on ESP32-PICO without PSRAM

modules.name: Task Scheduling
modules.description: Pluggable scheduler with Round-Robin and Priority FIFO classes. Supports SMP with per-CPU state. Three backends: FreeRTOS task container, native setjmp/longjmp (XEROS_NATIVE_SCHED), and POSIX ucontext (NATIVE_TEST).

modules.name: Virtual File System (VFS)
modules.description: inode/dentry/file three-level structure. Path resolution, per-task FD table, FD object pool with bitmap allocator. Supports open/close/read/write/ioctl.

modules.name: devfs
modules.description: Virtual filesystem for device nodes. Provides /dev/null, /dev/zero, /dev/random, /dev/ttyS0, /dev/gpio, /dev/led, /dev/buzzer, /dev/imu, /dev/screen.

modules.name: procfs
modules.description: Process information filesystem. Provides /proc/cpuinfo, /proc/meminfo, /proc/uptime, /proc/tasks. Uses esp_timer and esp_heap_caps for data.

modules.name: gpiofs
modules.description: GPIO pin access via filesystem. Uses Arduino GPIO APIs (digitalRead, digitalWrite, pinMode) and portMUX_TYPE for critical sections.

modules.name: Shell
modules.description: Interactive shell with built-in commands. Commands include ps, kill, ls, cat, echo, mkdir, touch, rm, date, reboot, ota, memtest, stack. Uses ESP-IDF OTA, NVS, and Arduino Serial APIs.

modules.name: MPU
modules.description: Memory Protection Unit support. ESP32 PMS register framework referenced; actual register operations marked TODO.

modules.name: Synchronization
modules.description: Spinlocks, mutexes, and condition variables. Uses atomic builtins and portMUX_TYPE on ESP32.

modules.name: Resource Tracking
modules.description: Per-task resource tracking for automatic cleanup on exit. Tracks FDs, memory, and custom resources.

modules.name: Port Layer
modules.description: Hardware abstraction layer. FreeRTOS backend is primary; native setjmp/longjmp backend is experimental. Contains dual-semaphore token protocol for scheduling.

modules.name: Memory Allocator
modules.description: Kernel memory allocation. Uses esp_heap_caps on ESP32, falls back to malloc on native.

modules.name: Task Manager
modules.description: UI application for task management. Protected from termination.

freertosCoupling.description: Primary FreeRTOS coupling. Dual-semaphore token protocol: scheduler gives token, task takes it, task gives done, scheduler waits on done. Task wrapper function bridges Xeros task entry to FreeRTOS thread.
SMP core identification and scheduler loop thread creation on Core 0.
SMP section only. Core 0 scheduler loop runs in FreeRTOS context.
Stack high water mark reading via port layer.
Critical section macros from FreeRTOS port layer (also available in esp-idf).
Critical section macros for serial device locking.

arduinoCoupling.description: Arduino HardwareSerial object for UART communication.
Included for cmd_date function; likely uses Arduino timing or serial functions.

notes: The port layer abstraction is well-designed: FreeRTOS coupling is almost entirely isolated to kern_port_freertos.c. The native setjmp/longjmp backend (kern_port_native.c) exists but is experimental and not currently compiled.

Migration to esp-idf FreeRTOS is straightforward because the current code already uses esp-idf FreeRTOS APIs (xTaskCreatePinnedToCore, xSemaphoreCreateBinary, etc.) rather than Arduino-ESP32 wrappers. The Arduino coupling is limited to GPIO and Serial operations.

Key API differences to watch for: (1) Arduino digitalRead/digitalWrite/pinMode should be replaced with esp-idf gpio driver (gpio_set_level, gpio_get_level, gpio_set_direction) in gpiofs. (2) Arduino Serial should be replaced with esp-idf UART driver (uart_write_bytes, uart_read_bytes) in dev_ttyS0. (3) portMUX_TYPE critical sections are compatible with esp-idf FreeRTOS and can remain.

The dual-semaphore token protocol in kern_port_freertos.c is the core scheduling mechanism. It relies on FreeRTOS task and semaphore semantics. Migrating to a different RTOS would require reimplementing this protocol, but staying within esp-idf FreeRTOS preserves it entirely.
ESP-IDF timer APIs (timer_init, timer_isr_callback_add, TIMERG0) are already used directly in kern_port_freertos.c and are fully compatible with esp-idf FreeRTOS.
ESP-IDF specific APIs used in shell and procfs (esp_ota_ops, nvs_flash, esp_system, esp_heap_caps, esp_timer) are already esp-idf native and require no changes.
The MPU implementation (kern_mpu.c) references ESP32 DPORT_PMS registers but is incomplete (TODO). This is hardware-specific and independent of FreeRTOS/Arduino.
SMP support uses xPortGetCoreID() which is available in esp-idf FreeRTOS. No changes needed.
Stack auto-growth feature is only implemented for native backends (NATIVE_TEST and XEROS_NATIVE_SCHED) and does not affect FreeRTOS builds.

options.name: LovyanGFX
pros: Upstream library of M5GFX with full ESP-IDF native support (CI validated)
Explicitly supports both ST7735 and ST7789 out of the box
Lightweight compared to LVGL; minimal RAM/flash overhead
FreeBSD license, active maintenance, large community
cons: Not a full GUI framework (no built-in widgets like buttons/sliders)
Requires manual UI element implementation if complex widgets are needed
options.recommendation: Primary recommendation for projects needing direct display control with good performance on resource-constrained devices.

options.name: LVGL
pros: Full-featured GUI framework with rich widgets, animations, and themes
Supports ST7735/ST7789 via drivers or esp_lcd integration
cons: LVGL v9 increased memory usage by ~33% over v8
Risk of memory exhaustion on 2MB flash devices without PSRAM (e.g., M5Stick-C)
Overkill for simple framebuffer or drawing tasks
options.recommendation: Only if the project requires complex UI widgets and the target hardware has sufficient RAM/flash (e.g., with PSRAM).

options.name: esp_lcd + custom drawing
pros: Uses ESP-IDF built-in components, no external dependencies
Minimal overhead if only basic display initialization is needed
cons: ST7735 is NOT included in esp_lcd; requires external component (e.g., waveshare/esp_lcd_st7735)
No high-level drawing primitives (lines, circles, text); must implement manually
Effectively requires building a custom framebuffer layer on top
options.recommendation: Acceptable for minimal projects where you only need to push raw buffers and are willing to implement all drawing logic yourself.

options.name: Custom framebuffer
pros: Maximum control and zero external dependencies
Minimal code size if scope is very narrow
cons: Must implement all drivers (ST7735/ST7789 initialization, SPI communication)
Must implement all drawing primitives and text rendering
options.recommendation: Not recommended unless the project has extremely unusual constraints or is an educational exercise.

mappings.notes: ESP-IDF uses gpio_num_t for pin numbers. Modes: GPIO_MODE_INPUT, GPIO_MODE_OUTPUT, GPIO_MODE_INPUT_OUTPUT. Requires gpio_install_isr_service() for interrupt-driven input.
Level: 0 (LOW) or 1 (HIGH). Must configure pin as output first with gpio_set_direction().
Returns 0 or 1. Pin must be configured as input (or input/output) first.
Requires adc_oneshot_new_unit() and adc_oneshot_config_channel(). ESP32-S3 has 2 ADC units with multiple channels. Use adc_cali for voltage conversion.
Requires ledc_timer_config() and ledc_channel_config() setup first. LEDC provides PWM. ESP32-S3 has 8 channels.
Same LEDC PWM mechanism as analogWrite. Set frequency and 50% duty for square wave tone.
Stops PWM output on the specified LEDC channel.
Requires gpio_install_isr_service(0) first. ISR runs in ESP32 interrupt context — keep it short, use FreeRTOS queues/semaphores for deferred processing.
Removes the ISR handler from the specified GPIO.
ESP-IDF v5.1+ uses new I2C driver. Configure scl_io_num, sda_io_num, clk_source. Legacy driver: i2c_driver_install() + i2c_param_config().

mappings.espIdfReplacement: i2c_master_transmit(i2c_master_dev_handle_t i2c_dev, const uint8_t *write_buffer, size_t write_size, int xfer_timeout_ms)
mappings.notes: Requires i2c_master_bus_add_device() to create device handle first. New driver uses device handles, not raw addresses.
ESP-IDF does not have streaming write. Accumulate data in a buffer and transmit in one call.
Combined write + transmit in ESP-IDF. Check return value for ACK/NACK errors.

mappings.espIdfReplacement: i2c_master_receive(i2c_master_dev_handle_t i2c_dev, uint8_t *read_buffer, size_t read_size, int xfer_timeout_ms)
mappings.notes: Read data in one call. Buffer must be pre-allocated. Returns ESP_OK on success.
Configure clock in bus config (new driver) or with i2c_set_clock_speed() (legacy). Standard: 100kHz, Fast: 400kHz.

mappings.espIdfReplacement: spi_bus_initialize(spi_host_device_t host, const spi_bus_config_t *bus_config, spi_dma_chan_t dma_chan)
mappings.notes: ESP32-S3 supports SPI2/SPI3 (HSPI/VSPI). Configure MOSI, MISO, SCLK pins. DMA channel SPI_DMA_CH_AUTO recommended.
Configure clock_speed_hz, mode (CPOL/CPHA), cs_io_num, queue_size in device config. Add device to bus for each chip select.
Fill spi_transaction_t with tx_buffer/rx_buffer, length (in bits). Call spi_device_transmit() for synchronous transfer.
Set trans.length = 16. Handle endianness manually if needed (ESP32 is little-endian).
ESP-IDF does not have explicit transaction begin/end. Bus is locked during transmit. Use spi_device_acquire_bus() for exclusive access if needed.
Yields to FreeRTOS scheduler. Minimum delay is 1 tick (configurable, usually 10ms). For shorter delays, use esp_rom_delay_us().
Busy-wait delay. Blocks the CPU. Use only for very short delays (< 10ms). For longer delays, prefer vTaskDelay().
Returns microseconds since boot. Divide by 1000 for milliseconds. Uses 64-bit to avoid overflow.
Returns 64-bit microseconds since boot. More precise than Arduino's 32-bit micros().
ESP32-S3 has 3 UARTs (UART_NUM_0, UART_NUM_1, UART_NUM_2). UART0 is typically USB/JTAG or external pins. Use uart_driver_install() for buffered I/O.

mappings.espIdfReplacement: uart_write_bytes(uart_port_t uart_num, const char *src, size_t size)
mappings.notes: Write to UART buffer. For USB Serial (CDC), use usb_serial_jtag driver or tinyusb. For printf-style, use ESP_LOGI() / ESP_LOGE().
Append CR+LF manually. Or use ESP_LOGI(TAG, "format", ...) which adds newline automatically.
Returns number of bytes in RX buffer. Alternatively use uart_read_bytes() with 0 timeout to poll.

mappings.espIdfReplacement: uart_read_bytes(uart_port_t uart_num, void *buf, uint32_t length, TickType_t ticks_to_wait)
mappings.notes: Read from UART buffer. Set ticks_to_wait to 0 for non-blocking. Returns bytes read or -1 on timeout.
Waits until TX FIFO is empty. Pass portMAX_DELAY to block until complete.

mappings.espIdfReplacement: Configure ticks_to_wait in uart_read_bytes() or use uart_set_rx_timeout()
mappings.notes: ESP-IDF uses FreeRTOS ticks for timeouts. Set per-read call rather than global timeout.
ESP-IDF power management: configure CPU frequency scaling, light sleep, deep sleep. Use esp_sleep_enable_timer_wakeup() for wake timers.
M5 devices use specific PMIC chips. ESP-IDF has no built-in PMIC abstraction. Use vendor-specific I2C commands or M5Unified's HAL layer ported to IDF.
IP5306: write 0x01 to reg 0xEA. AXP2101: configure via I2C. Requires reading PMIC datasheet.

mappings.espIdfReplacement: adc_oneshot_read() on battery ADC pin, or PMIC register read
mappings.notes: Many M5 devices have battery voltage on a GPIO via voltage divider. Read with ADC. Some PMICs report voltage directly via I2C.
Configure wakeup source (timer, GPIO, touch, ULP) before entering deep sleep. Use esp_light_sleep_start() for lighter sleep.
ESP-IDF LCD driver: esp_lcd_new_panel_io_spi() or _i2c(), then esp_lcd_new_panel_xxx() for specific controllers (ILI9341, ST7789, etc.).

mappings.espIdfReplacement: ledc_set_duty() on GPIO connected to backlight (PWM)
mappings.notes: Most LCD backlights are controlled via PWM on a GPIO. Configure LEDC timer/channel for backlight pin.

mappings.espIdfReplacement: esp_lcd_panel_draw_bitmap() with full-screen buffer, or fill buffer in memory then flush
mappings.notes: ESP-IDF LCD driver is low-level. Higher-level: use LVGL (lv_disp_drv_t) with esp_lcd backend. Fill buffer with color, then draw.

mappings.espIdfReplacement: Custom Bresenham line algorithm writing to framebuffer, then esp_lcd_panel_draw_bitmap()
mappings.notes: ESP-IDF LCD driver does not provide drawing primitives. Use LVGL, or implement Bresenham/graphics algorithms manually on a frame buffer.

mappings.espIdfReplacement: Custom rectangle draw to framebuffer, then flush
mappings.notes: Same as above — use LVGL for high-level graphics, or implement manually on framebuffer.

mappings.espIdfReplacement: Fill region in framebuffer, then esp_lcd_panel_draw_bitmap() for dirty region
mappings.notes: LVGL handles this automatically with esp_lcd backend. For raw ESP-IDF, manage framebuffer and flush dirty regions.

mappings.notes: Directly maps. Ensure bitmap format matches panel color format (RGB565, RGB888, etc.).

mappings.espIdfReplacement: LVGL style text color (lv_style_set_text_color()) or custom font renderer
mappings.notes: ESP-IDF has no built-in font/text rendering. Use LVGL for text, or integrate a font library (stb_truetype, freefont).

mappings.notes: LVGL uses lv_obj_set_style_text_font() with predefined font sizes. Or scale bitmap fonts manually.
LVGL handles text rendering, layout, and display. Create a label object, set text, and LVGL refreshes it.
LVGL positions objects absolutely or within layouts. For raw framebuffer, track cursor position manually.
ESP-IDF LCD driver provides swap_xy, mirror_x, mirror_y for rotation. Or handle rotation in software (LVGL can rotate display).

mappings.espIdfReplacement: esp_lcd_panel_draw_bitmap(panel, x, y, x+w, y+h, data)
mappings.notes: Direct equivalent. Ensure data format and endianness match panel expectations.

mappings.espIdfReplacement: Configured panel dimensions (stored in app context) or LVGL display driver resolution
mappings.notes: Track display dimensions in your application config. LVGL provides lv_disp_get_hor_res() / ver_res().

mappings.espIdfReplacement: memset(framebuffer, 0, size) + esp_lcd_panel_draw_bitmap() or LVGL screen clear
mappings.notes: Clear framebuffer to black/background color, then flush. LVGL: lv_obj_clean(lv_scr_act()) or fill screen with color.
LVGL is the recommended approach for text in ESP-IDF. For raw, use a bitmap font blitter.

mappings.espIdfReplacement: LVGL canvas draw triangle, or custom scanline rasterizer to framebuffer
mappings.notes: LVGL provides drawing primitives on canvas objects. Raw ESP-IDF requires implementing rasterization yourself.

mappings.espIdfReplacement: LVGL canvas draw arc/circle, or Bresenham circle algorithm to framebuffer
mappings.notes: LVGL has lv_canvas_draw_arc(), lv_canvas_draw_rect(). For raw, implement Midpoint circle algorithm.

mappings.espIdfReplacement: LVGL canvas filled circle, or scanline fill algorithm to framebuffer
mappings.notes: Same as drawCircle — use LVGL for simplicity, or implement fill in framebuffer.

mappings.espIdfReplacement: LVGL canvas, or custom ellipse rasterizer
mappings.notes: LVGL canvas supports arcs and rounded rects. Full ellipse may need custom rendering or approximating with arcs.
ESP-IDF has esp_jpeg component. Decode JPEG to framebuffer, then draw. Or use LVGL's built-in image decoder with libjpeg-turbo.
ESP-IDF does not have built-in PNG decoder. Include lodepng or similar, decode to RGB buffer, then draw.

mappings.notes: After esp_lcd_touch_read_data(), check if num_points > 0. LVGL handles this automatically via indev driver.
ESP32-S3 has I2S with PDM output for Class-D amplifier direct drive. Use i2s_std_config_t or i2s_pdm_tx_config_t. For DAC, use i2s_channel_init_std_mode() with built-in DAC.

mappings.notes: ESP-IDF I2S does not have built-in volume control. Scale samples in software (multiply by volume factor) before writing to I2S.

mappings.notes: Generate PCM samples for the tone, write to I2S TX channel. Use timer or task delay for duration. Or use ESP-ADF for higher-level audio.

mappings.notes: Parse WAV header, extract PCM data, write to I2S. ESP-ADF provides wav_decoder + i2s_stream elements for pipeline-based playback.

mappings.notes: Read raw PCM samples from I2S RX channel. Data is typically 16-bit little-endian. Apply gain scaling if needed.

Use POSIX stat() to check file existence. Returns 0 if file exists.
Standard POSIX remove/unlink after VFS mount.
LVGL's timer handler processes rendering and input. Run periodically in a task (e.g., every 5-10ms). Combine with touch read, button polling, etc.

mappings.notes: For physical buttons: GPIO interrupt + queue to task. For UI buttons: LVGL event system (lv_obj_add_event_cb()).

mappings.notes: ESP-IDF has no built-in IMU driver. Use vendor datasheets to configure registers via I2C. Or use ESP-BSP if available for specific board.

mappings.espIdfReplacement: I2C read from temperature register, apply datasheet conversion formula
mappings.notes: MPU6886: TEMP_OUT / 326.8 + 25.0. Varies by chip — check datasheet.

mappings.espIdfReplacement: Custom I2C driver for BM8563/PCF8563 RTC via i2c_master_transmit_receive()

mappings.espIdfReplacement: I2C read RTC registers (seconds, minutes, hours, day, month, year), convert BCD to binary

mappings.espIdfReplacement: I2C write RTC registers with binary-to-BCD conversion
mappings.notes: Reverse of getTime. Convert decimal to BCD ((val / 10) << 4 | (val % 10)), write to RTC registers.
Requires esp_netif_init(), esp_event_loop_create_default(), esp_wifi_init() first. Use event handler for IP_EVENT_STA_GOT_IP.

mappings.notes: No direct read API. Implement ring buffer in callback, consume from buffer in application code.

peripherals.espIdfApproach: Use the ESP-IDF GPIO driver with interrupt/debounce logic, or the official button component for event-driven handling (press, long press, double click).
peripherals.notes: Recommended: idf.py add-dependency "espressif/button^4.2.0". Supports GPIO and ADC buttons with built-in debouncing, event callbacks, and power-save mode.

peripherals.espIdfApproach: Direct I2C register read/write using ESP-IDF I2C master driver. Initialize I2C bus, then implement AXP192 register map for power control, charging, and LCD backlight.
peripherals.notes: No official ESP Component Registry driver exists. Reference the AXP192 header from nopnop2002's M5StickC ESP-IDF project. Key: use driver/i2c_master.h for ESP-IDF 5.x. Handles power rails, battery charging, and screen brightness via I2C.

peripherals.espIdfApproach: I2C communication using ESP-IDF I2C master driver. Implement register reads for accel/gyro data and configure scales/ranges.
peripherals.notes: Requires ROPG's I2C Manager component for thread-safe I2C operations. Clone from GitHub (m5stack/MPU6886-idf). Not in ESP Component Registry. Supports 6-axis data, FIFO, and interrupt configuration.

peripherals.espIdfApproach: Use ESP-IDF I2C driver to communicate with the BM8563 RTC chip for timekeeping and alarm functions.
peripherals.notes: Recommended: idf.py add-dependency "espp/bm8563^1.1.2". Clean C++ component with std::tm APIs. Alternative: esp-idf-lib/pcf8563 (idf.py add-dependency "esp-idf-lib/pcf8563^1.0.7") if you prefer C-style driver.

peripherals.espIdfApproach: M5StickC uses a simple buzzer (not I2S codec). Drive it via ESP-IDF LEDC PWM peripheral to generate tones, or use the I2S driver with internal DAC if using an external audio module.
peripherals.library: Built-in ESP-IDF LEDC driver (or esp_codec_dev for I2S codec boards)
peripherals.notes: For M5StickC's built-in buzzer: use ledc_set_duty() and ledc_update_duty() to generate square wave tones. For M5Stack CoreS3 (AW88298 I2S amp): use espressif/esp_codec_dev. Reference: nopnop2002/esp-idf-m5stack-speaker for PWM buzzer examples.

peripherals.espIdfApproach: Use ESP-IDF RMT or SPI peripheral to generate precise timing signals for addressable LEDs.
peripherals.notes: Recommended: idf.py add-dependency "espressif/led_strip^3.0.3". Official Espressif component supporting both RMT and SPI backends. Supports WS2812, SK6812, and similar addressable LEDs. DMA support available for large strips.

peripherals.espIdfApproach: Use ESP-IDF's official esp_lcd component with SPI interface for ST7789 display controller.
peripherals.notes: Recommended: idf.py add-dependency "jbrilha/esp_lcd_st7789^1.0.2" which implements the esp_lcd API. Alternative: clone nopnop2002/esp-idf-st7789 for a standalone driver with FONTX font support and frame buffering. M5StickC uses 80x160 or 135x240 ST7789 via SPI.

output.summary: Migrate M5Stick-P1 (Arduino/M5Unified framework) to xerintosh (ESP-IDF framework). The project uses a dual-implementation architecture (NATIVE_TEST vs hardware) with HAL abstraction layers. The kernel (Xeros) is already mostly ESP-IDF compatible (FreeRTOS APIs). Key migration targets: HAL display (M5GFX→LovyanGFX), HAL input (M5Unified buttons→GPIO), HAL system (Arduino millis→esp_timer), storage (Preferences→NVS), serial (Arduino Serial→UART driver), WiFi (Arduino WiFi→esp_wifi), GPIO (Arduino digitalRead/Write→gpio_driver), and build system (PlatformIO Arduino→ESP-IDF CMake). The UI/App layer has zero direct hardware dependencies and requires no changes.

phases.name: Phase 1: Build System & Project Skeleton
phases.description: Establish ESP-IDF build system, copy source tree, and create CMakeLists.txt structure matching the existing glob-based auto-registration but with explicit source lists for ESP-IDF.
steps: Copy entire src/ tree from M5Stick-P1 to xerintosh/src/
Replace xerintosh/src/CMakeLists.txt with explicit SRCS list (remove globbing for ESP-IDF compatibility)
Update xerintosh/CMakeLists.txt to include project.cmake and set C++17 standard
Create xerintosh/sdkconfig.defaults with CONFIG_FREERTOS_UNICORE=n, CONFIG_ESP32_DEFAULT_CPU_FREQ_240=y, CONFIG_ESP_CONSOLE_UART_DEFAULT=y
Update platformio.ini: change framework to espidf, add build_flags for -std=c++17, -Os, -fno-exceptions, -fno-rtti, and defines CONFIG_PREEMPT_ENABLED, CONFIG_SMP_ENABLED, CONFIG_MPU_ENABLED
Remove Arduino-specific lib_deps (M5Unified, M5GFX, ArduinoJson) from platformio.ini
Add LovyanGFX as an ESP-IDF component (git submodule or component directory)
Set up native test environment in platformio.ini with platform=native, test_framework=googletest, -D NATIVE_TEST

risks.description: ESP-IDF CMake does not support GLOB_RECURSE well; explicit file list required
risks.mitigation: Generate explicit SRCS list from existing file tree, update when adding files

risks.description: Native test environment may break if ESP-IDF headers leak into native builds
risks.mitigation: Keep NATIVE_TEST guard strong; all ESP-IDF includes must be inside #ifndef NATIVE_TEST

phases.name: Phase 2: HAL Display Migration (M5GFX → LovyanGFX)
phases.description: Replace M5GFX/M5Canvas with LovyanGFX (lgfx) for ESP-IDF. Preserve the 8-bit RGB332 framebuffer optimization (12.8KB RAM savings). Native path remains software framebuffer.
steps: Add LovyanGFX as ESP-IDF component (components/lovyangfx/)
Create LGFX config header for M5Stick-C (ST7735S 80x160, SPI pins, backlight GPIO 26)
Rewrite hal_display_fb.cpp hardware path: replace M5Canvas with lgfx::LGFX_Sprite, create sprite with 8-bit color depth
Rewrite hal_display_draw.cpp hardware path: replace g_canvas->drawPixel/drawLine/fillRect with lgfx sprite methods
Rewrite hal_display_font.cpp hardware path: replace g_canvas->setFont/drawString/textWidth/fontHeight with lgfx sprite methods
Rewrite hal_display_adv.cpp hardware path: replace g_canvas->readRect/pushImage/drawXBitmap/setClipRect with lgfx equivalents
Preserve cn_font subset (U8G2 font) integration with LovyanGFX
Ensure hal_display_flush() pushes sprite to LGFX display instance
Verify native path unchanged (software framebuffer continues to work)

risks.description: LovyanGFX API differs from M5GFX in sprite creation and color depth handling
risks.mitigation: Use lgfx::LGFX_Sprite with setColorDepth(8) and createSprite(w,h); test on hardware early

risks.description: 8-bit RGB332 color depth may render differently between M5GFX and LovyanGFX
risks.mitigation: Verify COLOR_FG/COLOR_BG/COLOR_ACCENT/COLOR_RED render correctly; adjust palette if needed

risks.description: Chinese font (U8G2 subset) may need adapter for LovyanGFX
risks.mitigation: LovyanGFX supports U8G2 fonts via setU8g2Font(); use lgfx::v1::U8g2font wrapper

phases.name: Phase 3: HAL Input & Power Key Migration
phases.description: Replace M5Unified button and AXP192 power key APIs with direct ESP-IDF GPIO and I2C drivers.
steps: Rewrite hal_input.cpp hardware path: replace M5.BtnA/BtnB with direct GPIO reads on GPIO 36 (BtnA) and GPIO 37 (BtnB)
Implement button debouncing and edge detection in software (replace M5.update() and wasPressed/wasReleased)
Preserve hal_input_double_click.c logic (pure C, no hardware deps)
Rewrite hal_power_key.cpp hardware path: replace M5.Power.getKeyState() with direct AXP192 I2C register 0x46 reads via ESP-IDF I2C master driver
Implement AXP192 I2C communication wrapper (i2c_master_transmit_receive) for power key state
Preserve power key state machine logic (timeouts, short/long/hold detection)

risks.description: GPIO 36/37 are RTC GPIOs on ESP32; direct gpio_get_level requires RTC GPIO initialization
risks.mitigation: Use gpio_set_direction and gpio_pullup_en appropriately; test on actual hardware

risks.description: AXP192 I2C address and register map may differ from M5Unified abstraction
risks.mitigation: Reference M5Stick-C schematic and AXP192 datasheet; verify I2C address 0x34

risks.description: Button edge detection timing may differ from M5Unified implementation
risks.mitigation: Match M5Unified debounce timing (~50ms); verify with oscilloscope if needed

phases.name: Phase 4: HAL System & Screen Migration
phases.description: Replace Arduino millis()/delay() with ESP-IDF esp_timer_get_time()/vTaskDelay(). Screen dimensions become runtime variables.
steps: Rewrite hal_system.cpp hardware path: replace millis() with esp_timer_get_time()/1000, replace delay() with vTaskDelay(pdMS_TO_TICKS(ms))
Keep native path using std::chrono unchanged
Verify hal_screen.c hardware path: g_screen_width/g_screen_height initialized by display driver (LovyanGFX) instead of M5.Display.width()/height()

risks.description: vTaskDelay may not provide sub-millisecond precision needed for some animations
risks.mitigation: Use esp_rom_delay_us for sub-ms delays; vTaskDelay for >1ms delays

phases.name: Phase 5: Storage Migration (Preferences → NVS)
phases.description: Replace Arduino Preferences library with ESP-IDF nvs_flash.h APIs. Preserve all key names and data formats for backward compatibility.
steps: Rewrite storage.cpp hardware path: replace Preferences with nvs_open/nvs_get_*/nvs_set_*/nvs_commit
Map all existing keys: wifi_count, bt_count, screen_orient, brightness, anim_speed, anim_enabled, spring_mode, spring_stiff, spring_damp, serial_baud_v1, ds_key_v1, flash_pin*
Preserve credential storage logic (cred_get_count, cred_get, cred_find, cred_add, cred_remove)
Ensure NVS namespace remains 'Xerintosh' for backward compatibility

risks.description: NVS string length limits and erase behavior differ from Preferences
risks.mitigation: NVS supports up to 1984 bytes per string; existing keys are well within limits

risks.description: Existing saved data on device will be lost if NVS namespace/key format changes
risks.mitigation: Preserve exact key names and value formats; data will be compatible

phases.name: Phase 6: Serial/UART Migration (Arduino Serial → ESP-IDF UART)

risks.mitigation: Use static buffer parsing or lightweight streaming parser; verify heap usage

phases.name: Phase 10: Main Entry & Kernel Integration
phases.description: Replace Arduino setup()/loop() with ESP-IDF app_main(). Integrate Xeros kernel initialization and task spawning.
steps: Rewrite main.cpp: replace setup()/loop() with app_main()
Initialize UART, I2C, SPI, NVS in app_main before other subsystems
Initialize LovyanGFX display instead of M5.begin()
Call storage_init(), settings_load_from_storage(), hal_display_init(), hal_system_init(), hal_input_init() in sequence
Call app_init_ui(), app_init_managers(), xerintosh_init_core()
Move deferred_kernel_init() content into app_main or a dedicated init task
Create UI task (ui_task_main) and WiFi task (wifi_mgr_task_main) using xTaskCreatePinnedToCore
Replace Arduino delay() with vTaskDelay in main loop
Remove Serial.begin()/Serial.println() debug outputs or redirect to ESP_LOG*

risks.description: ESP-IDF app_main runs as FreeRTOS task; stack size may be insufficient for init sequence
risks.mitigation: Increase main task stack in sdkconfig (CONFIG_ESP_MAIN_TASK_STACK_SIZE=8192) or do heavy init in a separate task

risks.description: Kernel timer ISR (sched_timer_isr) uses ESP32 timer_group0; may conflict with ESP-IDF system timers
risks.mitigation: Use timer_group1 instead, or use esp_timer for periodic callbacks

phases.name: Phase 11: Shell & Debug Cleanup
phases.description: Remove remaining Arduino.h includes from kernel shell and debug code. Ensure all ESP-IDF APIs are properly included.
steps: Remove #include <Arduino.h> from kern_shell_cmds.c (cmd_date uses esp_timer_get_time only)
Verify all ESP-IDF includes are present: esp_ota_ops.h, nvs_flash.h, esp_system.h, esp_heap_caps.h, esp_timer.h
Ensure debug_serial.cpp uses uart_write_bytes in hardware path
Verify kern_port_freertos.c FreeRTOS headers are compatible with ESP-IDF (freertos/FreeRTOS.h, freertos/task.h, freertos/semphr.h)

risks.description: Some Arduino macros may be implicitly used (e.g., constrain, map)
risks.mitigation: Audit all source files for Arduino macros; replace with standard C equivalents

phases.name: Phase 12: Testing & Verification
phases.description: Run native tests, build ESP-IDF firmware, and verify on hardware.
steps: Run native tests: pio test -e native
Build ESP-IDF firmware: pio run -e m5stick-c
Flash and verify: display init, button input, power key, WiFi scan, serial monitor, flasher, oscilloscope
Verify 8-bit RGB332 framebuffer works correctly with LovyanGFX
Verify NVS data persistence and backward compatibility
Run with sanitizers: cmake -DCMAKE_CXX_FLAGS='-fsanitize=address,undefined' for native tests

risks.description: Hardware testing may reveal timing differences between Arduino and ESP-IDF implementations
risks.mitigation: Iterate quickly: build, flash, test, adjust; use oscilloscope for timing verification

dependencies.name: LovyanGFX
dependencies.purpose: Replacement for M5GFX/M5Unified display driver with native ESP-IDF support, DMA SPI, ST7735S support, and sprite/8-bit color depth
dependencies.integration: ESP-IDF component in components/lovyangfx/ or PlatformIO lib_deps
dependencies.notes: Must configure LGFX config header for M5Stick-C (80x160, SPI, GPIO 26 backlight)

dependencies.name: cJSON
dependencies.notes: Lightweight; verify heap usage on ESP32-PICO

highRiskModules.risk: M5GFX→LovyanGFX API mismatch; 8-bit RGB332 framebuffer may render differently; Chinese font integration may break
highRiskModules.rollbackStrategy: If LovyanGFX fails, fallback to raw ESP-IDF SPI driver with custom ST7735S driver, or use M5GFX ESP-IDF port if available. Preserve native software framebuffer path as working reference.

highRiskModules.risk: Direct GPIO/AXP192 I2C may have timing/debounce differences from M5Unified; power key state machine may misdetect events
highRiskModules.rollbackStrategy: If direct GPIO fails, use M5Unified ESP-IDF port (if available) or reference M5Unified source for exact timing parameters. Add software debounce filters.

highRiskModules.risk: ESP-IDF WiFi scan/connect APIs have different semantics from Arduino WiFi; scan result caching and event handling may differ
highRiskModules.rollbackStrategy: Keep Arduino WiFi as ESP-IDF component (if possible) temporarily, or use esp_wifi APIs with explicit event loop. Test scan/connect thoroughly.

highRiskModules.risk: UART driver ring buffer behavior may differ from Arduino Serial; baud rate changes, bridge mode, and flasher DTR timing are sensitive
highRiskModules.rollbackStrategy: If ESP-IDF UART driver has issues, use driver/uart.h directly with custom ring buffers (already partially implemented). Preserve existing ring buffer architecture.

highRiskModules.risk: Arduino setup()/loop() to ESP-IDF app_main() transition may cause init order issues, task stack overflow, or watchdog triggers
highRiskModules.rollbackStrategy: Increase main task stack, defer heavy init to separate tasks, use vTaskDelay for yield. If critical, temporarily use Arduino as ESP-IDF component.
